objective: Construct a positive finite cubic girth-five witness against every fixed-radius punctured-map repair rule, auditing the homomorphism reformulation without changing the admitted target.

atomic_claims.text: For every r>=0, a positive connected cubic graph of girth five has a genuine punctured B-map with no repair fixing all labels beyond distance r.
Leaf-pinned full binary trees of every height h>=1 realize exactly any chosen nonadjacent two-label root set.
Two rooted tree lists A and D whose union neighborhoods are disjoint give an unextendable remote leaf assignment with a genuine punctured map.
The explicitly mapped 11-vertex one-port gadget has girth five and extends across a bridge to any prescribed outside target label.
The completed tree has 12*2^(h+2)+10 vertices; its cubicity, girth five, full positivity and original-vertex distances are preserved.

assumptions: The explicit target B has even five-bit vertices and generator edge differences J+e_i.
Only original tree leaves are pinned; union neighborhoods in the recurrence are not common-neighbor intersections.
The graph family is finite for each r, with h=max(1,r); ordinary source distance is used.
The root requires existential whole-graph coloring, unlike the universal punctured-map repair rule.
risks: The constructed graphs have bridges; cyclically four-edge-connected or minimal-counterexample subclasses are not covered.
No graph program, solver or verifier ran; recursive attainment is a paper proof.
B-map normalization need not preserve prescribed unnormalized original edge colors.
This auxiliary-rule failure is not a failure of the admitted equivalence route and is not root nonexistence.
